injuries.description: cervical spine condition / central cervical cord syndrome (whiplash-related cervical injury)
source: The QEH doctors at the Orthopaedics & Traumatology Department found his complaints were due to cervical spine degenerative changes with narrowing of C6 and C7 and corresponding intervertebral foramina and cervical spondylotic changes with posterior disc herniation at C3/C4 level that caused spinal cord compression.
Dr Chan considered the plaintiffs symptoms after the accident to be compatible with central cervical cord syndrome with predominantly sensory involvement, namely fingertip numbness.

manifestations.description: numbness of fingertips in both his hands
residual neck pain with stiffness on rotation and flexion
mild weakness and limitation of the left shoulder elevation and abduction
lack of strength in both arms
pain in the neck and shoulders
numbness in the base of his feet
would be able to drive but with less confidence and dexterity

treatments_received: treatment at the ICU of the Queen Elizabeth Hospital

losses.description: He is still suffering from pain in the neck and shoulders, stiffness of the neck, numbness of the fingertips, lack of strength in the left shoulder and left arm, numbness in the base of his feet.
